item.description: Abstract Geological constraints and modelling results reveal major yet poorly understood changes in Earth’s tectonic regimes during the late Archaean and Proterozoic. These changes are associated with supercontinent cycles, a primary archive of lithosphere and convecting mantle behaviour, and impact orogen duration and thermal state. However, the lack of precise data on orogen duration during Columbia assembly limits our understanding of the long-term tectonic evolution and comparison with younger orogens. Through in-situ garnet Lu–Hf and monazite microdomain U–Pb geochronology, here we constrain a 220 Myr hot collisional orogen during Columbia assembly, significantly longer than contemporary cold orogens (110–160 Myr). Secular changes in collisional orogen duration indicate a non-monotonic trend from Neoarchaean to Neoproterozoic. This trend implies enhanced plate rigidity and mobility during Columbia assembly, followed by a marked decline during Rodinia assembly, consistent with inferred plate velocity proxies. These findings support evolving tectonic regimes alternating between sluggish lid and more active plate tectonics during the Neoarchaean-Proterozoic. item.title: Mechanoradical hydrogen generation during seismic slip in an active fault zone
item.dc:creator: Yun Ya Ling

item.description: Black fault gouge identified in the rupture zone of the 2018 Hualien earthquake, Taiwan, bears abundant CaO and organic matter together with frictional melt, suggesting significant shear heating and natural hydrogen generation via mechanoradical reactions. Laboratory experiments and gas measurements suggest that rapid shearing in fault zones can trigger mechanoradical reactions that dissociate water and produce natural hydrogen. However, the lack of direct evidence means it is unclear whether this process operates in nature. We present mineralogical and microstructural observations of fault gouges recovered from the Milun Fault core three years after the 2018 M_W 6.4 Hualien earthquake in Taiwan. Quartz-rich yellow gouge contains clay and calcite but lacks carbonaceous material (CM). In contrast, black gouge contains crystallized frictional melt together with lime (CaO) and CM, suggesting that silicate minerals and calcite underwent shear heating during seismic slip. The formation of CM is experimentally associated with hydrogen-rich conditions, whereas lime is unstable in the presence of water. Therefore, the coexistence of lime and CM suggests formation under hydrogen-bearing and water-depleted conditions, consistent with mechanoradical reactions. Our results provide evidence of decarbonation and possible mechanoradical hydrogen generation during shearing in natural fault zones. item.description: Deep-time hyperthermal/transient warming events provide critical analogs for modern climatic warming and its impacts. item.title: Nitrification increases riverine nitrate delivery to changing Arctic fjord ecosystems
item.dc:creator: Andrew Hodson

Leah Jackson-Blake

item.description: Abstract Arctic fjords support important, productive ecosystems whose nutrient budgets are highly sensitive to climate-driven deglaciation. Here we present over three decades of data describing the nitrogen biogeochemistry of streamflow in the Kongsfjord and Adventfjord regions (West Spitsbergen, Svalbard) to show that microbial nitrate production by nitrification can substantially increase nitrate export to these fjords by runoff. Stable isotopes show that the nitrification of rock or “geogenic” nitrogen is particularly important, especially where shale-rich sedimentary rocks are present. In these cases, the release of nitrified nitrate into runoff may increase total riverine nitrate export by up to ~25 times, providing a potentially significant resource for utilization by downstream ecosystems. Since the influence of nitrification becomes more pronounced as ground thaw progresses, it could sustain primary production as the Arctic growing season lengthens, especially in nitrate-limited fjords. The widespread occurrence of shale bedrock across the Arctic also reveals a likely influence of geogenic nitrogen within the entire region. item.description: IIIE irons share geochemical characteristics with howardite-eucrite-diogenite meteorites suggesting both may have formed from differentiated planetesimal parent bodies, according to analyses on a silicate-bearing inclusion in the Aletai IIIE iron meteorite. Rocky planets formed through the differentiation of planetesimals into metal‑rich cores and silicate mantles, yet direct evidence linking these complementary reservoirs remains scarce. Here we show that IIIE irons and howardite-eucrite-diogenite (HED) meteorites are genetically linked, by integrating mineralogical, isotopic, and rare earth element (REE) analyses of the silicate-bearing Aletai IIIE meteorite. The silicates display Fe/Mn-Fe/Mg correlations, concordant oxygen isotope compositions, and strongly fractionated REE patterns consistent with those of HED meteorites. A pronounced negative Eu anomaly in orthopyroxene marks the onset of plagioclase saturation and buoyant segregation during early magma ocean crystallization, supported by thermodynamic modelling. These findings establish a genetic link between magmatic irons and differentiated achondrites, suggesting that IIIE irons and HEDs share a common genetic heritage, and providing direct physical evidence for core-mantle reservoir connections in the early Solar System. item.description: Internal solitary waves (ISWs) are powerful underwater disturbances that can vertically displace water by more than 200 meters, driving ocean mixing and affecting offshore engineering. Yet, their global distributions and vertical imprints remain poorly characterized. Traditional satellite sensors are constrained by cloud cover or limited sampling. The Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) mission provides near-continuous, cloud-independent ocean observations at unprecedented resolution. Here, we develop an artificial intelligence framework to automatically detect ISWs worldwide. Using 29 SWOT orbital cycles (July 2023 to March 2025), this study reveals a global map of ISW distribution and amplitude variations, identifying energetic hot spots and distinct seasonal and tidal variations. These findings provide insights into ISW dynamics and offer a foundation for assessing their role in global energy redistribution and ocean-climate interactions. item.title: Melt burst events in a dominantly amagmatic lithosphere at Gakkel Ridge in the Arctic Ocean
item.dc:creator: Fei Zhou
Ingo Grevemeyer
Jérôme Dyment
item.description: Abstract Alternation of magmatic and amagmatic seafloor along the slow and ultraslow spreading ridges is common. Yet, temporal variation is obscured by sediments blanketing oceanic basement away from spreading centers. Here we analyze aeromagnetic data covering zero age to ~35 Ma oceanic crust at the ultraslow-spreading Gakkel Ridge to characterize magmatic and amagmatic lithospheric domains and their links to melt supply. Amagmatic seafloor unexpectedly dominates ~68% of the Eurasian Basin, while only 32% of magmatic seafloor over the last 35 Ma. The melt supply exhibits cycles initiating over a short episode of robust magmatism followed by a longer intermediate magmatism, then starved magmatism. These observations suggest that strong lithosphere presumably characterizing this ultraslow spreading ridge may prevent a continuous melt supply, instead favoring episodic melt bursts. Our study indirectly constraints the extent and duration of melting events and lithospheric accretion through the Gakkel Ridge history, away from the present spreading axis. item.description: This study introduces a three-dimensional polarisation analysis method to deconstruct vibration waves from building blasting demolition, enabling separation of P, S, and R waves. Results reveal stage- and direction-dependent wave dominance, improving assessment and control of vibration hazards. Blasting demolition is widely used to remove large structures, but the resulting ground vibration can threaten nearby buildings and underground facilities. This vibration arises from explosive detonation and structural impact during collapse, giving it source mechanisms, wave components and attenuation behaviours that differ from those of underground blasting. Conventional peak and frequency indices cannot fully identify these contributions. In this study, a wave component characterisation method based on three dimensional polarisation states is developed to separate blast vibration waves from collapse vibration waves and analyse compressional, shear and Rayleigh waves during building blasting demolition. A normalised dominance factor is proposed to quantify wave type dominance and its transition during propagation. Here, we show that blast vibration waves exhibit staged changes in dominant wave components during initiation, whereas collapse vibration waves are controlled more strongly by shear and Rayleigh waves, supporting refined evaluation and control of blasting demolition vibration. item.description: Abstract Ferruginous conditions in the Precambrian oceans gave rise to ancient iron formations that contain the oldest recognized traces of life in the form of mineral biosignatures and isotope imprints. However, these biogeochemical archives lack clear constraints on microbial diagenesis prior to lithification as metabolic functions of the primeval subsurface biosphere remain elusive. item.description: Serpentinization, a widespread water-rock reaction in subducting slabs, profoundly influences the global water cycle and subduction dynamics. By integrating these feedbacks, we reconcile prior estimates and calculate a global slab mantle-derived water influx of 6 . 27 − 4.13 + 1.58 × 10 8 Tg/Myr. This corresponds to an effectively serpentinized fault network, rather than pervasive hydration, indicating that fault spacing and depth-dependent feedbacks are the primary tectonic controls on deep water cycling. item.description: Sulfur (S) in silicate melts exhibits complex behavior as a function of the oxygen fugacity and pressure, and its speciation and dissolution mechanisms are not fully understood. item.description: This study investigates the petrogenesis of Plio-Quaternary mantle-derived volcanic rocks emplaced across the Iranian Plateau, with a particular focus in determining the role of lithospheric thickness in modulating mantle melting processes. On the other hand, magmas produced above thicker lithospheric domains likely reflect smaller-degree melting at greater depths and possible interaction with enriched lithospheric mantle components that can generate more enriched incompatible trace-element contents and isotopic signatures, likely involving contributions from hydrous and/or carbonated sources. Crust assimilation is variably recorded in some volcanic suites from Iran, where trace element systematics deviate toward upper continental crust-like values. The data further suggest that transtensional tectonics and reactivation of strike-slip fault systems played a critical role in facilitating magma upwelling. item.title: An experimental study on the possible stability of whewellite CaC2O4·H2O under subduction zone conditions

item.description: Abstract Whewellite was reported as mineral in fluid inclusions in high-pressure metamorphic rocks, lending support to theoretical predictions that organic species may be stable and abundant in high-pressure subduction zone fluids. item.description: The Ivrea-Verbano Zone (IVZ, western Italian Alps) exposes a section of the lower continental crust and mantle where carbonatites have recently been identified. CO2-rich fluids played a critical role in mobilizing HFSE and REEs, which were subsequently incorporated into newly formed mineral phases. Crucially, whole-rock geochemistry and stable isotope signatures are inconsistent with a typical mantle carbonatite magma and instead support derivation from carbonate-rich protoliths subsequently modified by melt-rock interaction. item.description: The association of metal minerals in skarn deposits is common, including Cu-Mo, W-Sn, and Cu-Au systems. item.description: The genesis of ductile shear zones-hosted gold deposits remains controversial due to multi-stage mineralization and diverse ore sources. Rutile U–Pb dating yields ages of 178.8 ± 1.3 Ma (MSWD = 1.2; Stage I) and 177.1 ± 1.7 Ma (MSWD = 1.3; Stage III), constraining mineralization to the South China gold mineralization gap period (190–170 Ma), related to Paleo-Pacific Plate subduction. The Au-As-Cu-Pb-Ag-rich and oscillatory zoning of Py3a reflect fluid boiling during hydraulic fracturing, as corroborated by low δ34S values (avg. −1.24 ‰), hydrothermal breccias, and fluid inclusions observations. Ore fluids continuously migrated to Dagougu along the F0 fault zone, with pioneering fluids evolving at Dagougu and subsequent fluids gathering in F0. Hydraulic fracturing-induced pressure drops drove subsequent fluids into Dagougu. These fluids underwent intense fluid-rock interactions within F0, which is supported by F0 albitization, high δ34S values (avg. 10.21 ‰), and low Co/Ni ratios of Py3b. Reported H–O isotopes confirm fracturing-facilitated meteoric water infiltration. The resulting fO2 increase and cooling triggered gold precipitation, as evidenced by high Te in Py3b, low Mn in sphalerite, and low temperatures (148–185 ℃). Pyrite sulfur isotopes, published C–H–O isotopes, mineralization ages, and galena, pyrite, and albitite Pb isotopes suggest magmatic fluids derived from deep-mantle magma controlled gold mineralization through interactions with the Lechangxia Group. This study highlights the importance of magmatic-hydrothermal events in forming ductile shear zones-hosted gold deposits. item.description: The eastern Jiangnan Orogen is globally renowned for its large-scale tungsten mineralization but has historically been regarded as tin-poor. Recent exploration in northwestern Zhejiang has revealed significant tin mineralization within and around Heqiao granite, providing an opportunity to investigate Sn enrichment mechanisms in this belt. This study integrates geochronological, geochemical, and isotopic analyses of the Heqiao granite and its three distinct Sn mineralization types (granite-, greisen-, and stratiform quartz vein-type). Zircon U–Pb dating constrains the emplacement of the Heqiao coarse-grained granite at 124.7 Ma, while cassiterite U–Pb ages from all three mineralization types yield a tight cluster between 128 and 125 Ma, demonstrating a direct genetic link between magmatism and Sn mineralization. Whole-rock and biotite geochemistry, together with isotopic data indicate that the Heqiao granite is a highly fractionated, reduced A2-type granite derived primarily from partial melting of Mesoproterozoic metapelitic crust in an intraplate extensional setting. The granite exhibits elevated Sn content, strong fractional crystallization signatures, reduced redox condition, and enrichment in volatiles, collectively favoring Sn pre-concentration and hydrothermal mobilization. Cassiterite trace element compositions, particularly elevated Fe, W, and Zr/Hf ratios, together with their ages, consistently confirm a magmatic-hydrothermal origin for all three mineralization types, with the reduced nature of the ore-forming fluids having facilitated long-distance Sn transport and its ultimate precipitation within distal host strata. This study precisely defines a previously underappreciated Early Cretaceous Sn mineralization event in northwestern Zhejiang, and provides a new scientific basis for regional tin exploration. item.description: Understanding the structural controls and geochronology of diverse mineral deposit types, including iron oxide–Cu–Au (IOCG), porphyry Cu–Mo ± Au (porphyry), and epithermal vein-type (epithermal) systems within the Andean margin, remains a fundamental challenge in economic geology. This study integrates structural mapping, kinematic analysis, and geochronology to constrain the Cretaceous–Eocene tectonic evolution of the Coastal Range and Principal Cordillera in northern Chile (31° and 31°30′S) and its influence on the formation of El Espino (IOCG), Llahuín (porphyry cluster), and La Crucita (epithermal) systems. Our new data delineate three distinct tectonic stages. Stage 1 (Early to late Early Cretaceous, ∼135–115 Ma) was characterized by transtensional deformation along the NNW-trending Atacama Fault System, establishing the structural framework for subsequent IOCG mineralization in the El Espino district (∼93–86 Ma). Stage 2 (Late Cretaceous, ∼115–87 Ma) marked by positive tectonic inversion of Mesozoic extensional basins, during which pre-existing basin-margin normal faults were reactivated as reverse-oblique structures. A new Re–Os molybdenite age of 87.51 ± 0.23 Ma from Central Porphyry in the Llahuín porphyry cluster indicates that porphyry mineralization developed during this transpressional phase, approximately 4–5 Myr after formation of El Espino IOCG deposit. Stage 3 (Eocene, ∼45–35 Ma) reflects peak Incaic compression and significant crustal thickening. A new U–Pb zircon age of 40.7 ± 2.2 Ma from a granodiorite in the La Crucita district marks the southernmost expression of the Paleocene–Oligocene epithermal-porphyry metallogenic belt in this region. The distinct spatial and temporal distribution of IOCG, porphyry, and epithermal deposits reflects contrasting tectonic regimes, demonstrating that structural evolution exerted primary control on mineralization style and location. We conclude that inherited Mesozoic basin architectures, together with their subsequent tectonic inversion, imposed first-order controls on the timing and localization of mineral systems across the Andes orogen. item.title: Melt evolution during oceanic crustal accretion in the Central Indian Ridge revealed by gabbroic rocks from the Kairei hydrothermal field
item.dc:creator: Yuhong Fan

item.description: The magmatic-hydrothermal transition in the lower oceanic crust is critical for understanding crustal architecture and heat-chemical exchange at ocean ridges. Here we present petrographic, mineral-chemical, whole-rock geochemical, and trace-element modeling data for oxide-bearing gabbros and oxide gabbros from the active Kairei Hydrothermal Field, Central Indian Ridge. These rocks show progressive enrichments in Ti, Fe, and incompatible trace elements from oxide-bearing gabbros to oxide gabbros. Clinopyroxene Mg# values of 46–71 decrease with TiO2, Al2O3, Cr2O3, Ti/Dy ratios, and coexisting plagioclase anorthite contents, indicating progressive differentiation of Fe-Ti-saturated melts. Equilibrium melts calculated from clinopyroxene have low Mg# values of 10–34, much lower than regional basalts, implying derivation from highly evolved Fe-Ti-rich melts stored in deeper footwall reservoirs of the Kairei oceanic core complex. Their trace-element systematics further require extensive reactive porous flow during migration through lower-crustal crystal mush. Brown amphibole, with low Cl contents (<0.1 wt%) and crystallization temperatures of 740–870 °C, records late H2O-saturated trapped melts under near-solidus conditions, with limited seawater-derived fluid influence. In contrast, green amphibole rims around clinopyroxene record high-temperature hydrothermal overprinting <780 °C shortly after solidification. We propose that reactive processing of interstitial melts after basalt extraction concentrated highly fractionated Fe-Ti-rich liquids into the shallow footwall lithosphere to form Kairei oxide gabbros. These intrusions may supply heat and metals such as Fe and Zn, to sustain active seafloor venting and associated sulfide deposition.
